verdict: Meta's revenue jumped 33% to $56.3B on surging ads — and an $8.0B one-time tax benefit pushed net income up 61% to $26.8B.

segments.name: Advertising
segments.note: Ads across Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger: impressions grew 19% and the average price per ad rose 12%.

segments.name: Family of Apps other revenue
segments.note: WhatsApp business messaging, Meta Verified subscriptions and other app income; up 74% YoY.

segments.name: Reality Labs
segments.note: Quest headsets and AI glasses; sales dipped 2% and the unit lost $4.0B at the operating level.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: AI research (Meta Superintelligence Labs), engineers and Reality Labs development; up 46% YoY.

opex.name: Marketing & sales
opex.note: Selling ads and marketing Meta's apps and devices.

otherDetail: Meta reports one combined line, interest and other income (expense), net; this quarter it was a $1,120M net expense.
footerNote: The tax line is a $5,021M benefit: it includes an $8.03B one-time tax benefit (U.S. Treasury Notice 2026-7), partly offset by the quarter's normal tax charge.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Ads are surging
takeaways.text: Advertising revenue rose 33% to $55.0B: ad impressions grew 19% and the average price per ad rose 12%. The Family of Apps earned $26.9B of operating profit, while Reality Labs lost $4.0B.

takeaways.title: A one-time tax benefit inflated profit
takeaways.text: Net income includes an $8.03B tax benefit created by a U.S. Treasury notice on how the corporate minimum tax treats past R&D spending. Without it, EPS would have been $3.13 lower — $7.31 instead of $10.44.

takeaways.title: The AI build-out keeps accelerating
takeaways.text: Capital spending was $19.8B in the quarter, and Meta raised its full-year 2026 capex guide to $125-145B, citing higher component prices and more data-center capacity for future years.

oneTimers: An $8.03B income tax benefit (U.S. Treasury Notice 2026-7, on the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax treatment of previously capitalized U.S. R&D costs) is inside this quarter's tax line, turning it into a $5,021M benefit. It partly offsets the $15.93B non-cash tax charge Meta recorded in Q3 2025 when the One Big Beautiful Bill Act was enacted. Excluding the benefit, diluted EPS would have been $3.13 lower.
